request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Code has already chosen the configuration to carry forward with a paired fold rule; the choice and the paired comparisons behind it are under 'selection'. Your job is to decide whether more search is worthwhile and to flag concerns, especially any result that looks too good. You may request up to 2 more round(s) of experiments; propose configurations that could plausibly beat the current choice on paired folds, and set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. (Independent run 1.)

schema.description:
The choice of configuration is made in code (selection.py); the critic decides
whether to search further and flags concerns.

stop.description: true if no further experiment is justified
stop.title: Stop

schema.title: CriticVerdict

concerns: High ROC-AUC (~0.94) and PR-AUC (~0.735) relative to 9.35% baseline prevalence suggest potential feature leakage from aggregate provider size or claim volume features.
Undocumented origin of PotentialFraud label implies high metrics may reflect administrative patterns or proxy heuristics rather than audited fraud.
Limited search space explored so far (only 3 runs); Random Forest with agent features, LightGBM without class weighting, and Logistic baseline remain unexamined.

next_experiments.rationale: Evaluates LightGBM on the 'all' feature set without class weighting to directly compare against the leading Random Forest model.
Tests whether adding agent features enhances Random Forest performance beyond Run 2.
Establishes a baseline linear model to evaluate structural complexity vs risk of overfitting.
